title: Supporting FOSS projects to transition to memory safe tech — Tweede golf
excerpt: Sovereign Tech Agency have selected us as their partner for helping critical free and open source (FOSS) projects transition to memory safe tech like Rust, as part of their Sovereign Tech Resilience Program. In this article, we’ll go over the Program, why now is the right time to transition, and we’ll explain the basics of how FOSS projects can benefit from this collaboration, free of charge.
content_html:
We’re announcing, and honestly celebrating, the next chapter in our push for memory safety: Sovereign Tech Agency have selected us as their partner for helping critical free and open source (FOSS) projects transition to memory safe tech like Rust, as part of their Sovereign Tech Resilience Program. In this article, we’ll go over the Program, why now is the right time to transition, and we’ll explain the basics of how FOSS projects can benefit from this collaboration, free of charge.

We’re announcing, and honestly celebrating, the next chapter in our push for memory safety: Sovereign Tech Agency have selected us as their partner for helping critical free and open source (FOSS) projects transition to memory safe tech like Rust, as part of their Sovereign Tech Resilience Program. In this article, we’ll go over the Program, why now is the right time to transition, and we’ll explain the basics of how FOSS projects can benefit from this collaboration, free of charge.

The Resilience Program

The Sovereign Tech Agency are well-known in the FOSS ecosystem for their Sovereign Tech Fund, which does “strategic investments in the digital infrastructure of our economy and society”. In September 2026, they relaunched the Sovereign Tech Resilience Program, which works a little differently; STA has contracted suppliers to perform various services for FOSS projects, to strengthen the resilience of these projects. Unlike many grant programs in the industry, the Sovereign Tech Resilience Program does not give money directly to projects; instead it provides support from a paid-for engineering team.

So how does this program strengthen the resilience of FOSS projects? By “improving projects’ underlying capacity to prevent, withstand, and respond to [bugs]” in various ways (which you can read more about here), including by offering support for transitioning code bases to Rust, Go, or Python.

Transition to memory safety

That is where we come in. We’ve been contracted to support participating projects in transitioning codebases, whole or in part, from memory-unsafe languages such as C or C++ to memory-safe alternatives where appropriate.

The services we will be delivering to FOSS projects are:

  • assessing which components are suitable for rewrites
  • producing prioritized migration roadmaps
  • carrying out rewrites while maintaining functional equivalence and compatibility
  • training maintainers to keep developing the memory-safe components

Why now

A lot of our world depends on various critical open source projects. By now, it’s obvious that hardening these critical open source components, by investing in them and contributing to them, is important. As we’re currently seeing a surge in both (agentic) cyber attacks and AI-assisted vulnerability discoveries, this has become more pressing than ever before, and we’re not expecting this urgency to let up.

There are, thankfully, different ways to go about it, and many excellent initiatives (e.g. the Alpha Omega project), but here’s why we’re so excited to be a part of this one specifically:

  • The Programs’s criteria ensure a risk and impact based investment
  • A project’s maintainers stay in the lead
  • The effort is substantial enough (i.e. secured for at least 3 years) to create real and lasting impact

To us, being STA’s partner in this also presents a very tangible step in our advocacy for memory safety, which started in 2023 but has felt more pertinent each year since.

How to apply for this program

For FOSS projects that are interested, the process is very straightforward:

  1. Read the participation criteria
  2. Apply to the program
  3. Get selected
  4. Make a plan with STA and us, while you stay in the lead
  5. We collaboratively execute the plan

You can apply for one or multiple areas of support (aside from memory safety, think e.g. software supply chain security, security audits, and more). The resulting engagement can be large or small, long or short, depending on the services you’re interested in and that fit your project’s needs.

Questions?

We are currently working on several FOSS projects that are unrelated to the Resilience Program. If you’d like to know more about our open-source work first, here are some of those projects:

  • e-KS and Abacus, for the Dutch Electoral Council
  • Open Device Partnership for Microsoft
  • Various projects at Trifecta Tech Foundation, the non-profit that we founded in 2024 to develop and maintain digital commons, open-source software and open standards for the Internet and other vital systems. Projects range from time synchronization (e.g. ntpd-rs and sectime.org), to compression (e.g. zlib-rs) and privilege boundary (e.g. sudo-rs).

Any other questions? Please refer to the Program’s FAQ, or reach out to me, Hugo.

We’re thankful for the opportunity to work with various open source projects and maintainers in such a constructive way in the years to come. We look forward to working with you, to helping you get things done that were challenging before, and making a positive impact together!
